Day 27 of 100 · Infrastructure Automation

Ansible Inventory

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityInfrastructure AutomationPublished journey entry

Inventory is the model of what Ansible manages: hosts, groups and the connection data that lets automation reach the correct systems.

Architecture / mental model

inventory → groups / hosts → host variables → play host pattern

How it works

An inventory can be static or dynamic, but its job is the same: identify managed hosts and organize them into useful groups.

Groups should model real operational boundaries such as web, database, environment or region rather than becoming arbitrary buckets. Group membership then becomes reusable targeting logic.

Connection variables belong only where necessary. Keeping target identity and connection assumptions explicit prevents a playbook from silently reaching the wrong machine.

Hands-on reference

ansible-inventory -i inventory.ini --graph
ansible-inventory -i inventory.ini --list

Verification

Render the inventory graph and confirm every host belongs to the groups you expect before running a broad play.

Field note / gotcha

A typo in a group name can produce a perfectly valid pattern that matches zero hosts. 'Nothing changed' may mean 'nothing was targeted.'

Security considerations

Keep private keys and credentials outside inventory files. Inventory often ends up in source control and should be safe to publish internally.

What I learned

Targeting starts with an accurate model of the fleet.
